name: Synergy QMP
description: Bilingual training and certification portal for the Transportation of Dangerous Goods, Class 7. Students study, take a timed exam, and download their certificate, while admins manage everything from a dashboard.
overview: Synergy QMP provides online training and certification in the Transportation of Dangerous Goods, Class 7 (radioactive materials) for nuclear medicine, radiopharmacy, and research staff across Canada. Students sign in, read the course material, take the exam, and download a certificate their employer can trust.

Their existing platform was a WordPress site from 2017 paired with a separate PHP application for exams. The plugins no longer received security fixes, course PDFs and the exam answer file could be downloaded by anyone with the link, and student passwords were stored as unsalted MD5 hashes. I rebuilt it as a single Next.js application with a modern public site, a student area, and a full admin panel, all in English and French.
keyFeatures: Fully bilingual (English and French) with locale prefixed routes
Timed exams with answers saved as you go and server enforced time limits
Certificate PDFs generated in the course language with unique certificate numbers
Course material served only to signed in, enrolled students
Admin dashboard with charts, user management, CSV import, question banks, and an audit log
Light and dark mode admin panel
Old URLs forwarded to their new pages to preserve search rankings
Deployed on Vercel with database migrations applied during production builds
challenges: The biggest challenge was moving over years of existing data without disrupting active students. The legacy MySQL database held more than 1,200 students, 1,500 enrollments, 860 past exam attempts, and the full question bank, spread across two systems with inconsistent structure.

I wrote a migration script that parses the legacy dump, builds a migration plan, and produces a report before anything is written. Dry runs against a separate database branch let me rehearse the migration until every past answer was matched to its question. Passwords were the trickiest part. Rather than forcing every student to reset, the new auth layer verifies the old MD5 hash on first sign in and transparently upgrades it to modern hashing.

The exam itself also needed to be reliable. Students often take it between clinical shifts, so a dropped connection or accidental refresh could not cost them an attempt. Each answer is saved to the server as it is selected, the attempt resumes exactly where it left off, and the deadline is enforced on the server rather than trusting the browser's timer.
Finally, everything had to work in two languages from the start. Every page, email, exam, and certificate exists in both English and French, and the language switch keeps students on the same page.
outcomes: Synergy QMP now runs on a single, maintainable platform instead of two aging systems. The security issues of the old site are gone: course material and exam content are only available to enrolled students, passwords are properly hashed, and each admin has their own account with every change recorded in an audit log.

Every existing student moved over with their history intact and could sign in with their existing password. Admins can now add students in bulk, adjust exam rules, edit question banks, and reissue certificates on their own, without developer involvement.

name: South West Exposures
description: Medical isotope shield catalog and inquiry system. Custom admin content management system for adding, updating, and deleting products.
overview: South West Exposures is a specialized engineering and technology firm focused on creating innovative shielding solutions for sectors that work with advanced drug therapies and radiological materials.

They came to me with an existing WordPress website that no longer reflected the quality or sophistication of their work. The site suffered from poor SEO performance, inconsistent structure, and an outdated user interface that made it difficult for visitors to quickly understand their products and expertise. They wanted a completely new look and feel for the UI, along with a stronger foundation for search visibility. Just as importantly, they needed the ability to easily add and manage their own content, rather than relying on static, hard-coded pages, so their site could grow and evolve alongside the business.
keyFeatures: Product catalog with filters and sorting
Responsive design for mobile and desktop
SEO optimized with dynamic meta tags
Deployed on Vercel with automated CI/CD
challenges: A major early challenge was sourcing the right creative talent to support the new design direction. The project required both a UI/UX designer to help shape the user experience and a 3D renderer to create high quality product imagery that accurately reflected SW Exposures’ offerings.

I collaborated closely with two specialists who brought deep expertise to the project. UI and UX design was led by <Link href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/adamrwood">Adam Wood<Link/>, while 3D product rendering was handled by <Link href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/sony-chen-48433b135">Sony Chen<Link/>. Their combined work made it possible to clearly present complex, highly technical products through a clean and consistent visual system.

Another key challenge was choosing a technology stack that could support long term growth while significantly improving SEO performance. The previous site struggled with search visibility and limited flexibility for modern optimization techniques.

Next.js was selected as the foundation for the rebuild due to its performance and SEO advantages. PostgreSQL was used as the primary database to support structured, scalable content management and future expansion. Each product page was implemented with dynamic meta tags to improve search relevance, and an automated sitemap was generated and submitted to Google Search Console. This combination created a fast, SEO focused platform that allows for easy content updates and long term maintainability.
outcomes: Following launch, the new site delivered measurable improvements in performance, visibility, and engagement. Search visibility increased significantly, with indexed pages growing by over 60 percent and several core product pages beginning to rank within the top 10 to 20 results for relevant industry search terms. Dynamic metadata and a properly structured sitemap helped accelerate indexing through Google Search Console.

Customer engagement also improved. Overall site traffic increased by approximately 40 percent, while average time on site increased by 30 percent, indicating that users were more effectively finding and exploring relevant content. Clearer navigation and improved product presentation reduced friction for visitors and made it easier to understand SW Exposures’ offerings.

Operationally, the new platform reduced content update time by an estimated 98 percent, allowing the team to add new products and make changes without developer involvement. The scalable Next.js and PostgreSQL architecture now supports ongoing SEO optimization, future product expansion, and long term growth without the limitations of the previous system.

name: Fitzsystems
description: Software development business website. Designed to provide information on services, showcase projects, and setup a line of communication for potential clients.
overview: Fitzsystems is my software development business where I design and build software solutions. I have plans to launch other SAAS products under the Fitzsystems brand, so I created a strong foundation for future growth and expansion.
keyFeatures: Responsive design for mobile and desktop
challenges: The main challenge for this project was creating a clean, modern design that effectively communicated my services and expertise without overcomplicating the development process.
To address this challenge, I leveraged V0 to create a ShadCN inspired design. I was able to iterate over versions and tweak the design to my standards and needs.
Another major challenge was the hero section background animation. I was unable to find a suitable design, even with the use of V0.

I came up with the idea of having my companies logo falling from the top of the page. After tweaking with the colors, sizes, and animation, I was able to create a unique and eye catching animation that fit the design of the site and my brand.
